---
title: "Choropleth map"
description: "An sf object drawn directly with mark_sf() and a proper map projection via coord_sf()."
categories: [Spatial]
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
```

vellumplot reads simple-features geometry directly. `mark_sf()` draws the polygons
and `coord_sf()` handles the projection and aspect ratio.

For a version you can hover, select, and zoom, see the
[interactive choropleth](choropleth-interactive.qmd).

```{r}
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)

p <- vplot(nc, width = 8, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_sf(fill = BIR74) |>
  coord_sf() |>
  labs(title = "Births by county, North Carolina (1974)", fill = "births")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p, "choropleth")
```

## Dissolving the borders between equal values

Bin the values and a per-feature choropleth starts to lie about its own geometry.
Neighbouring counties in the same class are drawn as separate polygons, so a border
is stroked twice down the middle of what should read as one region: a visible seam,
and in PDF an exact one.

`mark_sf(merge = TRUE)` dissolves adjacent features that share a fill into a single
region. The union is real boolean geometry (`vellum::vl_path_op()`), holes and
multipart features preserved, so each region comes out as one crisp path rather than
a stack of alpha-composited neighbours.

```{r}
nc$class <- cut(nc$BIR74, breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000, 4000, Inf),
                labels = c("under 1k", "1k–2k", "2k–4k", "over 4k"))

p_merged <- vplot(nc, width = 8, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_sf(fill = class, merge = TRUE) |>
  coord_sf() |>
  labs(title = "Birth classes, merged into regions", fill = "births")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p_merged, "choropleth-merged")
```

Compare it with the same classes drawn feature by feature. Same colours, but every
county boundary is still there, including the ones between counties of the same
class:

```{r}
p_unmerged <- vplot(nc, width = 8, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_sf(fill = class, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) |>
  coord_sf() |>
  labs(title = "The same classes, one path per county", fill = "births")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p_unmerged, "choropleth-unmerged")
```

`merge` is ignored on an interactive layer, and necessarily so: merging throws away
the per-feature keys a widget needs to know which county you hovered.

For the cartographic furniture (a scale bar, a north arrow, a graticule) see
[Scale bar, north arrow, graticule](map-decorations.qmd).

## Two variables on one map

A bivariate choropleth colours each county by two variables at once. `bi_class()`
cuts both into terciles and `scale_fill_bivariate()` maps the nine
combinations onto a two-dimensional palette. `guide_bivariate()` labels the
swatch edges with the class breaks, and `rotate = TRUE` turns the key into a
diamond with low-low at the bottom and high-high at the top.

```{r}
nc$sids_rate <- 1000 * nc$SID74 / nc$BIR74
nc_bi <- bi_class(nc, BIR74, sids_rate)

p_bi <- vplot(nc_bi, width = 8, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_sf(fill = bi_class, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) |>
  coord_sf() |>
  scale_fill_bivariate(palette = "GrPink", xlab = "births",
                       ylab = "SIDS per 1,000") |>
  guides(fill = guide_bivariate(rotate = TRUE, labels = TRUE,
                                xlab = "births", ylab = "SIDS per 1,000")) |>
  labs(title = "Births and SIDS rate, North Carolina (1974)")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p_bi, "choropleth-bivariate")
```
